tips.intro: Bubble Up Endless is a bubble shooter where you fire colored bubbles up into a cluster that hangs from the top of the screen. These tips come from several real runs, with scores from a few hundred up to 50,150.
tips: Check the small bubble beside the launcher before you shoot. It shows the color coming next, so you can save a spot for it instead of being surprised.
The aiming line takes the color of the bubble you are holding. Use it to confirm the color and the exact landing spot before you let go.
Go for the bubbles that hold a big section in place. When the support goes, everything below it drops loose, and in one run that took the score from 850 to 3,400 in a single shot.
Loose bubbles fall into five buckets along the bottom worth 50, 100, 150, 100 and 50 points. Drops in the middle are worth the most.
Clear on back-to-back shots to keep the multiplier in the top right climbing from x1 to x2 and x3. A shot that pops nothing resets it to x1.
Keep the red dashed line above the launcher in view. If the cluster reaches it, the run ends with FAILED.
When the cluster gets close to the red line, stop chasing combos and clear the lowest row first.
tips.conclusion: Read the next bubble, line up a clean match and protect the red line. Big scores come from drops and multipliers, not from risky shots.

extra_sections.heading: How the multiplier and buckets add up
paragraphs: Every bubble that falls lands in one of the buckets along the bottom, worth 50, 100 or 150 points depending on where it lands. The multiplier in the top right corner rises when you clear on consecutive shots.

That is why one well-placed shot that drops a large hanging section is worth far more than several small pops. In one run the score went from 850 at x1 to 3,400 at x2 and then 6,250 at x3 over a few connected clears.

extra_sections.heading: When the cluster starts to sink
paragraphs: Shots that pop nothing stick to the cluster, so it grows down toward the red dashed line. Once it gets close, play two or three safe shots that pop low groups, even if they score little.
With some space back, go back to looking for supports that drop big sections.

controls.intro: Bubble Up Endless uses a single action. You press and hold to aim, then release to fire. The game shows this as an on-screen hint at the start of a run.
controls.desktop: Press and hold the left mouse button in the play area, then move the cursor to swing the dotted aiming line. Release the button to fire. The pause button sits in the lower left corner. No keyboard controls were needed or listed.
controls.mobile: The on-screen hint reads Tap and hold to aim. Then release to shoot, which suggests holding a finger down to aim and lifting it to fire. Touch controls were not tested, since all testing was done with a mouse, so play on a touch screen is unconfirmed.
tips: Keep holding while you adjust. The shot only fires when you let go, so there is no penalty for taking time to aim.
The menu has music, information and sound buttons along the bottom.
Accept the notice that appears when the game first opens, then press Play.

beginner-guide.intro: New to Bubble Up Endless? This guide walks through what is on the screen and how to play your first run without filling the board.
beginner-guide.what_it_is: Bubble Up Endless is a free bubble shooter that runs in your browser. A cluster of blue, green and orange bubbles hangs at the top of the play area and you fire bubbles from a launcher at the bottom. Fire into groups of the same color to pop them, and any bubbles left with nothing holding them up fall into point buckets. A progress bar at the top counts toward a total of 230, and the run ends with FAILED if the cluster reaches the red dashed line.
first_steps: Press Play on the title screen. Your best score shows just below the button.
Read the hint, Tap and hold to aim. Then release to shoot, and fire a couple of easy shots into matching groups.
Look at the small bubble next to the launcher to see the color that comes next.
Aim for spots where your bubble touches two or more of its own color.
Watch the score at the top center and the multiplier in the top right after each clear.
Use the pause button in the lower left corner if you need a break.
beginner-guide.who_its_for: Anyone who likes calm, turn-by-turn puzzle games with a score to chase. There is no time pressure, so it suits players new to bubble shooters as well as regulars.

extra_sections.heading: Reading the screen
paragraphs: Across the top you will see a coin counter on the left, your score in the middle, a progress bar such as 10/230 with a gift icon beside it and the multiplier on the right. The buckets along the bottom show their point values, 50, 100, 150, 100 and 50.
Below the buckets is a bar with the pause button and four booster buttons marked with a plus sign. What each booster does was not tested, so this guide sticks to normal shots.

similar.intro: Bubble Up Endless is about aim and planning rather than speed. You choose when to shoot, read the next color, line up shots along the dotted aiming line and look for the one bubble holding up a big section. If you enjoy that calm, shot-by-shot style and the payoff of a big drop into the point buckets, try more puzzle games from the Pixelsprout catalog next. Look for games where you match colors at your own pace and a single good move can clear a large part of the board.

faqs.question: How do you shoot in Bubble Up Endless?
faqs.answer: Press and hold to aim, move to adjust the dotted aiming line, then release to fire. The game shows this as a hint at the start of a run.

faqs.question: How do you lose in Bubble Up Endless?
faqs.answer: The run ends with FAILED when the bubble cluster reaches the red dashed line just above the launcher.

faqs.question: What are the buckets at the bottom for?
faqs.answer: Bubbles that fall loose drop into five buckets worth 50, 100, 150, 100 and 50 points. The middle bucket pays the most.

faqs.question: What does the x2 or x3 in the corner mean?
faqs.answer: It is the score multiplier. It rises when you clear bubbles on consecutive shots and drops back to x1 after a shot that pops nothing.

faqs.question: Can you see the next bubble?
faqs.answer: Yes. A small bubble beside the launcher shows the next color, and the aiming line takes the color of the bubble you are about to fire.

faqs.question: What does the bar at the top count?
faqs.answer: It is a progress bar that counts up toward 230 as you play, shown as values like 10/230, with a gift icon at its end.

faqs.question: Is there a time limit?
faqs.answer: No timer was shown while playing. You can take as long as you want to line up each shot.
